payload.comment:
Ingestion stage is structurally sound: loaded split sizes (89996/10004/7180) match official sizes exactly, subsampled=false, all three index SHA-256 hashes are present, archive MD5 is recorded, and no artifacts were omitted. The test-domain note (CRC-VAL-HE-7K from a different clinical center) is properly documented and should be carried forward into any downstream evaluation reporting.

One reproducibility concern warrants attention: llm_model_digest is null while llm_mode=ollama and llm_model="qwen3.8" are set. If the LLM participates in any pipeline step (e.g., label refinement, prompt-based augmentation, or evaluation commentary), the absence of a pinned model digest means the exact weights/version cannot be reproduced from the manifest alone. Recommend capturing the ollama model digest (or at minimum a content hash of the GGUF/weights file) before proceeding to training or evaluation stages. This does not block ingestion, but it should be resolved before any stage that consumes LLM output.

Minor observations (non-blocking): (a) the model name "qwen3.8" deviates from the typical Qwen integer/one-decimal naming convention; verify it resolves to the intended checkpoint in the ollama registry. (b) The archive integrity check uses MD5 while index files use SHA-256; acceptable for a download checksum but worth standardising on SHA-256 in future schema revisions. (c) All package versions (torch 2.14.0+cu126, numpy 2.4.6, lightning 2.6.5, etc.) are internally consistent with the 2026-09-08 timestamp and the Linux/glibc platform string.

No deterministic findings were raised. Proceed to the next stage, but ensure the LLM digest gap is closed before any LLM-dependent computation is executed.
llm_issues: llm_model_digest is null while an LLM (qwen3.8 via ollama) is declared in the run manifest; exact model weights are not pinned, undermining full reproducibility of any LLM-dependent step
llm_model name 'qwen3.8' is atypical for the Qwen naming convention; verify it maps to the intended checkpoint in the ollama registry

Test split originates from a different clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K); domain shift is documented but must be explicitly reported in all downstream evaluation metrics to avoid conflating in-domain and cross-domain performance
